newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian PM defends Merrill Lynch t-bill deal.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian PM defends Merrill Lynch t-bill deal.

text.p: Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Stankevicius on Tuesday defended a deal to sell U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch some 200 million litas of government Treasury bills, local news agencies said.
The bills, with a maturity of one year, were sold to Merrill at a rate of 22 percent. Opposition leader Vytautas Landsbergis said domestic banks would have accepted 15 percent.

"The loan by Merrill Lynch was granted in litas. Therefore, this is a good way for our securities to enter the global financial market," Stankevicius, quoted by domestic news agency ELTA, told a news conference.
He said local banks were once demanding rates near 40 percent although the rates had now fallen to about 10 percent.
Yields on Lithuanian paper soared at the start of the year after a banking crisis.
"Now, yields have fallen naturally to 10 percent only because funds have started coming in from abroad," the Baltic News Service (BNS) quoted Stankevicius as saying.
Stankevicius also rejected accusations he had personally profited from the deal with Merrill.
"I can just shrug my shoulders as I neither received any share nor did anybody ever offer it to me," ELTA quoted Stankevicius as saying.
Landsbergis' accusations came as Lithuania heads for parliamentary elections on October 20 in which the ruling Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party (LDLP) is expected to lose.
